text:
emma_cs: Quick sync — Lighthouse dedicated pool backlog popped overnight, wanted to drop a short snapshot and next steps. cc @raj_infra @maya_ops @sasha_csm :eyes:

raj_infra: Infra snapshot from 03:00–08:00 UTC: reserved_hours=720h/month, used_last_7d=512h (71%), avg_hourly_saturation=68%, peak_saturation=94% (03:12 UTC), avg_queue_depth=6, max_queue_depth=21. Spike aligns with nightly eval runs. Link: https://redwood-ops.internal/dashboards/lighthouse/pool

maya_ops: noted. The max queue depth of 21 is the one we flagged last week as a potential SLA risk (p99 latency > 1.2s). Do we have which tenant jobs caused the peak?

raj_infra: quick query we ran: ```sql
SELECT tenant, sum(gpu_seconds) as gpu_s FROM job_events WHERE ts >= now() - interval '8 hours' GROUP BY tenant ORDER BY gpu_s DESC LIMIT 10;
-- top: lighthouse-evals (~42%), lighthouse-batch-analytics (~18%), misc-tenant (~6%)```

oliver_se: thanks — looks like the nightly evals are the main culprit. Lighthouse confirmed they ramped up evaluation suites last week (new model variant). That explains the burst. Renewal note: they have a renewal in ~5 weeks and finance pinged Sasha about unexpected spend.

sasha_csm: confirm — I had a finance call earlier. They're happy with latency currently but worried about "surprise" overages from burst traffic. Renewal is in 35 days, so it'd be good to present mitigation options.

deploy-bot: ALERT: pool lighthouse-dedicated queue_depth > 20 at 2099994354 (auto-throttle engaged) :warning:

emma_cs: Proposed short-term mitigations: 1) ask Lighthouse to move non-critical evals to off-peak window (2–5am PST) 2) enable temporary burst capacity + cap per-tenant concurrency 3) schedule enablement call to review batching/caching and suggest quantization for eval runs.

oliver_se: For engineering: I can prepare a config change to cap concurrent eval workers to 8 and add prefix caching for repeat prompts. Also can provision +200 burst GPU-hours for the next 7 days if CS approves. Impact: should drop max queue depth below 10 based on our sim.

maya_ops: Ops checklist: - apply concurrency cap (owner: raj_infra) - provision burst (owner: oliver_se) - cost projection + email to finance (owner: sasha_csm) - confirm scheduled time window for non-critical jobs (owner: emma_cs). Aim to complete within 48h.

raj_infra: I'll push the concurrency cap to staging now and roll to canary. Patch snippet: ```yaml
pool: lighthouse-dedicated
concurrency_limit_per_tenant: 8
burst_hours_allocated: 200
```
Rolled at 2099994460 to canary, monitoring p99.

sasha_csm: I'll draft a short note for their finance team outlining temporary burst and proposed long-term options: right-size reserved commit vs buy bursts. Also prepping renewal talking points: retention priority is reliability + predictable cost.

emma_cs: Can we get a quick post-action summary for the customer before EOD tomorrow? If the sim on canary looks good, we'll propose a 30-minute enablement session Tue 10:00 PT.

oliver_se: Canary sim: projected p99 latency down from 1.25s to 0.48s, estimated cost delta +6% this week for burst hours. If that looks ok, I'll provision to prod at 2099994680.

raj_infra: Prod change applied at 2099994680. Immediate telemetry shows queue_depth dropping: now avg 3, max 9. Keeping watch for next 24h.

sasha_csm: Finance note sent. They asked for an estimate if we instead increased reserved by 15% vs bursts — will collate numbers and share in the enablement call.

emma_cs: Great. Next steps recap (48h):
- raj_infra: verify canary->prod stability and confirm metrics (p99, queue_depth)
- oliver_se: finalize burst provisioning and config docs for Lighthouse ops
- sasha_csm: finance comparison + renewal talking points
- emma_cs: schedule enablement + get Lighthouse agreement on off-peak run window

maya_ops: I'll own a follow-up check-in next Friday to see if utilization stabilizes and to surface any residual renewal risk.

oliver_se: thumbs up. I'll upload the small runbook snippet to the shared drive: https://redwood-share/internal/lighthouse/runbooks/gpu-backlog.md

emma_cs: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread for the log. Please post short updates here once your step is done. :thumbsup:
